title: Chunky
tagline: I run the website for our yearly golf weekend, and I make the shirts and swag.
what: The Chunky Invitational is a golf weekend around 20 of my friends do every year. I run its website, where everyone signs up, picks a shirt size and a bag-tag nickname, and pays. I also do the shirts, and I make the bag tags and coasters on my 3D printer.
built: This year's site: sign up, pick a shirt size and a bag-tag nickname, then pay by Venmo
An admin page with who's paid and the shirt count by size, which the shirt order comes from
Shirt art for the front and back, traced into clean one-colour files for screen printing
Code that turns the signup list into one print file per person
A nameplate for the trophy, printed at home, so nobody had to find an engraving shop
credit: I run the site and make the swag

making.problem: Around 20 people have to sign up, pay, and end up with a shirt in the right size and a bag tag with their own nickname, all in a few weeks.
how: Everyone registers on the site with a shirt size and a nickname
They pay by Venmo and I mark them paid
The shirt order comes straight from the size count
A script builds each person's bag tag file from their nickname

broke.title: A plate in four hours
broke.body: A plate of coasters came down from about 14 hours to about 4 after I corrected the filament settings in the code that builds the print files.

credits: The Chunky logo carries over from earlier years
This year's shirt art and the coaster art started as ChatGPT images, the coaster one from a friend's photo
I turned them into the files that got printed

moment.what: I texted the group that registration was open at about 1:45 in the afternoon. By 3:30, five people had signed up, with their shirt sizes and nicknames.
